record.title: Golela–Lavumisa export suspension during June 2021 Eswatini unrest
record.scope: South Africa-to-Eswatini exports at Golela–Lavumisa; wider reported frontier interruptions remain separate scope leads.
record.direction: South Africa to Eswatini, export traffic.
record.movement: Exports from South Africa through Golela; the record does not extend the customs notice to all passengers or imports.
record.exceptions: No exception to the specified export suspension documented; other movement categories are not established.
record.imposing_authority: Border authorities; SARS notified the export suspension and reporting describes Eswatini military guarding the crossing. Exact issuing authority and chain of command not recovered.
record.enforcement: Dated SARS suspension notice and contemporaneous reporting of the guarded closure.
record.relationship: Promotes the Golela component of R4-AES-L003. Related to the unrest setting of R4-AES-001, but distinct crossing and date. Mananga’s June 29/July 1 overlap in R4-AES-L001 remains unresolved; no second Mananga episode added.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; no inference of status at the 2026-10-21 cutoff.
record.official_rationale: SARS bulletin gives no reason. Unrest and contestation of royal rule are reported context, not an attributed customs justification.
record.context: Pro-democracy protests and coercive responses disrupted Eswatini’s frontier access. Contemporary reporting describes this crossing shut for much of June 29 under military guard.
record.uncertainty: No reopening recovered. The bulletin dates Golela exports June 29, but broader closure causes and modes differ by post. Do not infer a continuous nationwide or passenger closure, or extend status to the bulletin’s July 2 update date.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. No duration: export-specific onset/status June 29; actual end unknown.
